veteran.description: A veteran is a person who has long experience in a particular field, usually combat. Veterans are often found leading hunting parties, protecting enclaves or escorting Technicians through the perilous wilds. They have valuable knowledge of the wastelands that is hard-earned and well protected
veteran.name: Veteran

warden.description: A Warden is more than just a leader to their people. They understand the resources and maintenance requirements of their enclave and how the decisions they make affect the region. They are responsible for the security of their enclave and enforcing any regulations. In the face of danger, they are skilled negotiators but they also know when deadly force is required.
warden.name: Warden

dragon.description:
Instead of facing the slow and lumbering hordes of the walking dead you may want a foe that has fewer numbers and facing even one foe poses the likelihood of defeat.

No other mythological creature has received as much attention as the dragon. Tales of dragons are known in many cultures and were believed to be real for centuries. It's not clear where these tales originated but, huge flying serpents with venomous breath have been described in texts as early as the ancient Greeks and Sumerians. The belief in dragons was not just founded in legend but also in physical evidence. The knowledge of dinosaurs would not come for millennia and people would attribute the huge fossilised bones to those of dragons.

Tales of dragons ranged from being watchful protectors to malicious hunters. When Christianity spread dragons took on a solely sinister interpretation and came to represent Satan. The mouth of a dragon was at this time first depicted to breathe fire and was a symbol of the entrance to hell itself. The church even created their own legends of righteous saints battling and vanquishing Satan in the form of dragons. Dragons are, in fact, one of the only monsters whose purpose is that of a fearsome opponent to be slain.

As such, dragons make a superb foe to bring about the end of the world
dragon.name: Dragon

hulk.description: The Hulk is a zombie that has been supersized. The Revenant pathogen is known to regenerate tissue. Not perfectly, but it keeps the dead walking. Muscle regrowth is achieved through hypertrophy. This happens when muscles sustain damage or injury and the body repairs them by fusing them. This creates larger and stronger muscles. In a Hulk, the pathogen has focused on rebuilding muscle tissue too well.
hulk.name: Hulk

runner.description:
The runner isn't technically a zombie, yet. They're a human that's been infected with the Revenant pathogen and are presently affected by the first stage. You can't reason with them. You can't hope against all odds that the person they once were will shine through. Hell, you can barely even outrun them. A runner will expend its total energy without reserve. It won't wait patiently for someone to cross their path. They run. And run. And run.

Runners are why the Revenant pathogen spread so quickly. These vectors would run full tilt until they encountered their prey. Then, once they catch up to them, they'll try to tear them limb from limb. The pathogen enters the victims' blood and soon they'll also go through Stage 1 and join the hunt.
runner.name: Runner

handful_of_runners.description: A small amount of 3-5 Runners are roaming together.
handful_of_runners.name: Handful of Runners

pack_of_runners.description: A larger amount of 6-10 Runners are roaming together in a pack.
pack_of_runners.name: Pack of Runners

sable.description:
A sable is the result of a mutation in a zombie brain. When it's ready, or when circumstances force it, the sable will form by pushing the zombies black blood into the cranium. This will cause it to explode and any large chunks of brain matter is then drawn into the blood. 

Sables then search out a new host and, when it enters them, begins to change their anatomy. The Revenant pathogen starts by taking control of the central nervous system and, once it has finished, goes to work on rebuilding the host's sinew and collagen.
features: Chunks of brain floating in it
sable.name: Sable
tactics: Enter the body through an orifice

sable_host.description:
Initially a the host of a sable may try to verbally communicate with others and warn them away. This is because the pathogen has taken control of the body, but not completely. The host will try to flee to isolation and safety. Once it has undergone the last of its changes it will rejoin its previous companions.

Eventually, a sable-host is stronger and smarter than they were before and, is capable of totally replicating the host's mannerisms and remembering their memories. Due to their increased intelligence, a sable-host will wait for an opportune moment to feed and try to remain undetected.
sable_host.name: Sable-host
tactics: Hide until in control of the host

screamer.description:
Screamers have mutated to form massive packs of the undead. A normal zombie moan can call their kin from only a short distance. Even so, when one moans and another hear it, they moan and so on and so forth.

The screamers can call other zombies from kilometers away. Their chest cavities are massive and reinforced with enough sinew and cartilage that they have been know to stop low-powered ammunition.

When you see a screamer, you better hope you see it before it sees you or you're in for a lot of trouble.
screamer.name: Screamer

spitter.description: The contents of a zombie's stomach is a cesspool of bacteria and disease. Touching a zombie's skin alone would be enough to require a range of medications. A spitter zombie is one that has mutated the ability to regurgitate the contents of their stomach with such force that it sprays up to two meters. It then uses the distraction as an advantage to gorge itself upon its victim and refill the now empty stomach.

You may also apply these features like a template to any of the NPC's listed under the 'Animal Kingdom' section if you want the Revenant pathogen to be capable of reanimating creatures other than humans.

You can roll more than once to add additional details.

combat_action.summary: Use this oracle to help inspire an action for an NPC in combat. When you're not sure what your foe does next, particularly when you are in a bad spot, roll on this table and interpret the result as appropriate to the situation. If this oracle isn't appropriate for a character, consider using the [Combat Method](datasworn:oracle_rollable:revenant/character/combat_method) and [Combat Target](datasworn:oracle_rollable:revenant/character/combat_target) oracles.

combat_method.name: Combat Method
combat_method.summary: Use this table to answer questions about the actions of of a foe or enemy force. You can use these oracles instead of, or in addition to, the [Combat Action](datasworn:oracle_rollable:revenant/character/combat_action) oracle. Roll once each on the [Method](datasworn:oracle_rollable:revenant/character/combat_method) and Target oracles. Then, interpret the response as appropriate to the current situation and the nature of your foe.

combat_target.name: Combat Target

initial_disposition.name: Initial Disposition
initial_disposition.summary: Use this oracle when you want to define the initial tone of an encounter with an NPC.

name.name: Character Name
name.summary: The name of a character might be the first or last detail revealed. You may only know a person's name and begin an arduous hunt to find them or, you might meet a lone traveller in the wasteland and only after revealing other details of the encounter would you learn their name.

character.name: Character Oracles

action.name: Action

Then, interpret the result based on the context of the question and your current situation.

descriptor.summary: This oracle is similar to the [Action](datasworn:oracle_rollable:revenant/core/action) and [Theme](datasworn:oracle_rollable:revenant/core/theme) oracles. They are abstract word prompts you can use to generate the details of a location or event, or to answer questions about it's nature. A roll on this table can be combined with a [Focus](datasworn:oracle_rollable:revenant/core/focus) to provide an adjective and a noun.

focus.name: Focus
focus.summary: As with the [Descriptor](datasworn:oracle_rollable:revenant/core/descriptor) oracle, this is an interpretative table which you can use to answer questions or generate new situations. Combined, the Descriptor and Focus tables provide creative prompts suitable for most locations and events.

theme.name: Theme
theme.summary: As with the [Action](datasworn:oracle_rollable:revenant/core/action) oracle, this is an interpretative table which you can use to answer questions or generate new situations. Combined, the Action and Theme tables provide creative prompts suitable for most

location.name: Location Oracles
location.summary:
Locations are places. The world around you, whatever state it's in. To create a location you will envision the area. You will determine the landscape, the hazards or the opportunities the location provides, and other features of the area.

Each location on the following pages includes a set of oracles.
  * __Feature__: Use this oracle to reveal a new aspect of the location.
  * __Hazard__: Use this to oracle help envision a complication or hazard.
  * __Opportunity__: Use this oracle to help envision a beneficial encounter or event, or when you roll a strong hit with a match.

The location oracles are divided territories and themes. A territory is an oracle to help you envision a biome or district. Themes help you envision the motif or atmosphere of a location.

story.name: Story Oracles
story.summary: The following oracles fill niche roles, but still provide useful resources to inspire your imagination.

endurance.description: Health represents your current physical condition and stamina.
endurance.label: endurance

morale.description: Morale is your current mental state.
morale.label: morale

radiation.description: Radiation represents your current protection level against radiation.
radiation.label: radiation

supply.description: Supply is an abstract representation of your preparedness, including ammunition, provisions, fuel, medicine, tools, and general upkeep.
supply.label: supply

permanently_harmed.description: Permanently harmed may be marked when you are at 0 endurance and fail to [Endure Harm](datasworn:move:revenant/suffer/endure_harm). You have suffered a wound such as the loss of an eye or hand. Or you bear physical scars which serve as a constant reminder of a harrowing incident.
permanently_harmed.label: permanently harmed

traumatized.description: Traumatized may be marked when you are at 0 morale and fail to [Endure Stress](datasworn:move:revenant/suffer/endure_stress). Your experiences have left you emotionally scarred.
traumatized.label: traumatized

lasting_effects.description: Lasting effects are permanent. They forever impact your character through the momentum adjustment and - more importantly - the narrative impact of being permanently harmed or traumatized. You should factor this impact into how you perform moves and how you interact with the world.
lasting_effects.label: lasting effects

encumbered.description: Encumbered is marked as appropriate to the circumstances when you are carrying excessive or cumbersome weight.
encumbered.label: encumbered

irradiated.description: Irradiated is marked when you are at 0 radiation and fail to [Endure Radiation](datasworn:move:revenant/suffer/endure_radiation). You suffer acute radiation syndrome, and need comfort to recover.
irradiated.label: irradiated

shaken.description: Shaken (Dispirited) may be marked when you are at 0 morale and fail to [Endure Stress](datasworn:move:revenant/suffer/endure_stress). You are despairing or distraught, and need comfort to recover.
shaken.label: shaken

unprepared.description: Unprepared is marked when you [Sacrifice Resources](datasworn:move:revenant/suffer/sacrifice_resources) and are reduced to 0 supply. You and your allies share the same supply value, and will mark unprepared together.
unprepared.label: unprepared

wounded.description: Wounded may be marked when you are at 0 endurance and fail to [Endure Harm](datasworn:move:revenant/suffer/endure_harm). You are severely injured and need treatment to recover.
wounded.label: wounded

misfortunes.description: As with all impacts, misfortunes affect your max momentum and momentum reset. In addition, if you are wounded, shaken, or unprepared, you cannot increase the associated condition meter.
misfortunes.label: misfortunes

battered.description: Battered may be marked when your vehicle is at 0 integrity and you fail to [Withstand Damage](datasworn:move:revenant/suffer/withstand_damage). The vehicle is barely holding together.
battered.label: battered

vehicle_troubles.description: Vehicle troubles are linked to a specific vehicle. These impacts are only a factor when you are piloting or aboard that vehicle. Otherwise, they do not count as an impact and do not affect your maximum momentum and momentum reset values.
vehicle_troubles.label: vehicle troubles

plans_legacy.label: plans

edge.label: edge

heart.label: heart
